tools.name: phone_lookup
tools.description: Check a user-provided phone number for carrier and line type. Optional US/CA caller-name data is a carrier listing, not identity verification. Uses existing account credits: 1 for landline/VoIP/toll-free, 3 for mobile or unknown; caller name adds 2. Reserves up to 5 credits before execution. Does no

tools.name: email_verify
tools.description: Check an email address supplied by the user for syntax, MX records, disposable-domain and role-address indicators. Does not prove mailbox ownership or guarantee delivery. Uses 1 existing account credit for a successful check; does not send email.

tools.name: ip_lookup
tools.description: Look up approximate IP location and network/provider indicators for an IP address supplied by the user. IP location is not a person's precise location or identity; privacy flags may be unavailable. Uses 1 existing account credit for a successful check.

tools.name: dns_check
tools.description: Inspect a user-provided domain's MX, SPF, DMARC or DKIM record and report issues. Does not change DNS. DKIM requires a selector. Uses 1 existing account credit for a successful check.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: phone_lookup, email_verify, dns_check · Private data: email_verify, dns_check · Public sink: phone_lookup, email_verify.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: phone_lookup, email_verify, dns_check · Private data: email_verify, dns_check · Public sink: phone_lookup, email_verify

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
